title: The Langevin Diffusion in Continuous Time
source_sections: 1.4 The Langevin SDE as a Wasserstein Gradient Flow (p. 31)
goal: Build the analytic language that turns Langevin dynamics into quantitative convergence estimates.
prerequisites: Conditional expectation and elementary Markov-process notation
core_definitions: A Markov semigroup evolves observables by conditional expectation.
The infinitesimal generator is a time-zero semigroup derivative on its stated domain.
The overdamped Langevin SDE has drift minus the potential gradient and isotropic Brownian noise.
The Wasserstein gradient-flow viewpoint identifies the Fokker-Planck evolution with entropy dissipation.
major_results: Itô's formula yields the formal Langevin generator.
The weighted integration-by-parts calculation predicts the Gibbs stationary density.
Poincaré and log-Sobolev inequalities turn dissipation identities into exponential convergence.
Strong convexity supplies the condition-number-dependent convergence scale summarized at the end of the chapter.

calculation_route.formula:

calculation_route.explanation: Itô's formula identifies the first-order change of expectations. The displayed operator is only a formal generator until a function domain is fixed.

calculation_route.title: From the generator to dissipation
calculation_route.explanation: The cancellation explains symmetry and entropy/variance dissipation. ASTIS treats the integration-by-parts passage as a theorem chain, not as notation.

calculation_route.title: From a functional inequality to convergence
calculation_route.explanation: Differentiate the variance along the semigroup, insert the Poincaré inequality, and solve the scalar differential inequality.

rigorous_details: The weighted integration-by-parts identity first needs compactly supported test functions or a justified cutoff limit.
Pointwise exhaustion of a cutoff does not imply convergence of its gradient term under an integral.
A totalized Fréchet derivative equal to zero outside a support set does not assert differentiability there.
The score-weighted source field must be integrable before dominated convergence can be applied.
Formal symmetry, a closed generator on a stated domain, stationarity, and invariance are separate claims.
blockers: Concrete Langevin Markov semigroup construction (external/upstream dependency)
Semigroup-stable generator-domain extension beyond the compiled C_c^2 core
Full invariant Gibbs law and measure-determining extension
consumers: Discretization analyses for LMC and ULMC
recommended_order: Open the cutoff and integrability detail packets

title: Functional Inequalities
goal: Develop Poincaré, log-Sobolev, transport, and isoperimetric tools, including semigroup proofs and preservation operations.
core_definitions: Poincaré inequality: variance is controlled by Dirichlet energy; the compiled local interface records probability normalization, its test class, and all three integrability requirements explicitly.
Log-Sobolev inequality: relative entropy is controlled by Fisher information.
Talagrand transport inequalities compare relative entropy with Wasserstein distance.
Isoperimetric and concentration profiles quantify boundary expansion and tail decay.
major_results: Markov-semigroup interpolation proves functional inequalities from curvature and dissipation.
Tensorization, bounded perturbation, Lipschitz pushforward, and other operations preserve selected inequalities with tracked constants.
Functional inequalities imply concentration and isoperimetric estimates.
The framework extends, with changed analytic interfaces, to manifolds and discrete chains.

calculation_route.title: Curvature gives a coercive scale
calculation_route.explanation: Strong convexity supplies the characteristic length and time scales used by Langevin algorithms.

calculation_route.title: Boundary expansion controls variance
calculation_route.explanation: An isoperimetric lower bound is converted into a functional inequality.

rigorous_details: State whether Hessian inequalities hold everywhere, almost everywhere, or in a weak convex-analytic sense.
Track normalization and absolute continuity whenever a potential is used to define a probability law.
Keep localization inputs separate from the one-dimensional inequality they reduce to.
blockers: Bakry–Émery Poincaré criterion, pending a concrete semigroup/generator domain

title: Additional Topics in Stochastic Analysis
source_sections: 3.2 Change of Measure in Path Space (p. 99)
goal: Build the stochastic-analysis tools used later for path-space comparison, conditioned diffusions, and bridge constructions.
prerequisites: Basic stochastic calculus for the Girsanov route
core_definitions: Quadratic variation records the second-order accumulation of path increments.
The stochastic exponential is the path likelihood used for drift changes.
A Doob transform conditions or tilts a Markov evolution through a positive space-time function.
Föllmer drift and the Schrödinger bridge formulate entropy-minimizing path-space transports.
major_results: Brownian quadratic variation produces the correction in Itô calculus.
Girsanov's theorem identifies the law of a process after an adapted drift change.
Doob's transform gives a conditioned generator and semigroup.
Föllmer and Schrödinger constructions connect relative entropy, optimal drift control, and endpoint constraints.

calculation_route.title: Identify stochastic quadratic variation
calculation_route.explanation: Quadratic variation is the correction term that distinguishes stochastic calculus from ordinary calculus.

calculation_route.title: Change a drift by a path likelihood
calculation_route.explanation: Girsanov's theorem turns drift control into an absolute-continuity statement on path space; Doob and Föllmer transforms specialize this idea.

rigorous_details: Quadratic-variation limits require an explicit convergence mode and partition scheme.
A stochastic exponential needs measurability and integrability conditions before it defines a change of law.
Finite-dimensional cylinder identities are not automatically path-space Girsanov theorems.

title: Analysis of Langevin Monte Carlo
goal: Derive Langevin Monte Carlo guarantees through Wasserstein coupling, interpolation, convex optimization, and Girsanov comparison.
core_definitions: Langevin Monte Carlo is the Euler discretization of overdamped Langevin diffusion.
A synchronous coupling shares Brownian noise between two trajectories.
A continuous interpolation embeds the discrete chain into an SDE with frozen drift.
Girsanov comparison measures the interpolation error at the path-law level.
major_results: Wasserstein coupling yields contraction plus a one-step discretization bias.
Interpolation arguments control terminal error through a differential inequality.
A convex-optimization analogy recovers a sampling convergence estimate.
Girsanov's theorem converts integrated drift mismatch into a divergence bound for LMC.

calculation_route.title: Couple two trajectories
calculation_route.explanation: Strong monotonicity of the drift produces contractivity.

calculation_route.title: Compare drifts by path likelihood
calculation_route.explanation: The drift mismatch becomes a time-integrated quadratic cost.

rigorous_details: The coupled processes must be constructed on one filtered probability space.
Path-space laws and filtration-adapted drift differences must be explicit.
Optimization analogies do not replace stochastic existence or integrability assumptions.

title: Faster Low-Accuracy Samplers
goal: Study randomized midpoint, Hamiltonian, and underdamped methods that improve low-accuracy complexity.
core_definitions: Randomized midpoint uses an internal random evaluation time to reduce discretization bias.
Hamiltonian Monte Carlo alternates approximate Hamiltonian flow with momentum refreshment.
Underdamped Langevin evolves position and momentum with friction and noise.
Hypocoercive metrics couple position and momentum errors.
major_results: Randomized midpoint improves the low-accuracy dimension dependence over basic Euler discretization.
Hamiltonian trajectories exploit second-order phase-space motion before refreshment.
Underdamped Langevin contracts in a suitable mixed metric under strong log-concavity.
Discretized accelerated dynamics produce faster low-accuracy sampling guarantees under stated smoothness and step-size regimes.

calculation_route.title: Lift position into phase space
calculation_route.explanation: The auxiliary velocity changes contraction and discretization behavior while preserving the desired position marginal.

rigorous_details: Invariant phase-space laws require both position and momentum normalization.
Hypocoercive estimates mix position and velocity norms; coercivity is not pointwise in the position coordinate alone.
Exact Hamiltonian flow and numerical integrators must not be conflated.

title: Convergence in Rényi Divergence
goal: Analyze LMC and ULMC in Rényi divergence using interpolation and Girsanov arguments.
core_definitions: Rényi divergence is the logarithmic power integral of a density ratio at a chosen order.
LMC and ULMC interpolations are continuous processes agreeing with the discrete algorithms at grid times.
Local drift error is the squared discrepancy between the true and frozen or discretized drift.
major_results: LMC admits a Rényi-divergence analysis through interpolation.
A Girsanov route controls LMC by an integrated drift mismatch.
The underdamped analogue requires phase-space moment and drift-error bounds.
The final complexity estimates balance continuous convergence, divergence order, and step size.

calculation_route.title: Balance mixing and discretization
calculation_route.explanation: Choose the horizon for mixing and the step size for approximation, then optimize both.

calculation_route.title: Measure the frozen-drift error
calculation_route.explanation: Smoothness converts increments of the process into a Girsanov cost.

rigorous_details: The interpolated chain must be adapted and have the same diffusion coefficient as the comparison process.
Moment estimates must be established before integrating local drift error.
Step-size restrictions and all dimension/condition-number constants must be retained.
recommended_order: Convert path divergence to terminal error

title: High-Accuracy Samplers
goal: Use accept/reject correction and conductance tools to obtain exact-target chains.
core_definitions: A rejection sampler accepts a proposal using a density-envelope ratio.
The Metropolis-Hastings filter corrects a proposal kernel through a reversible acceptance ratio.
Conductance measures the one-step flow across measurable cuts.
A warm start bounds the initial density ratio relative to stationarity.
major_results: The Metropolis-Hastings correction preserves the target through detailed balance.
Conductance and warmness convert local proposal quality into global mixing.
MALA obtains high-accuracy guarantees from both cold and warm initializations under different smoothing arguments.
Acceptance estimates determine the stable step-size and complexity regimes.

calculation_route.title: Correct a proposal
calculation_route.explanation: The acceptance ratio restores detailed balance with the target.

calculation_route.title: Turn local movement into mixing
calculation_route.explanation: Conductance and warmness control the global number of steps.

rigorous_details: Kernel measurability and exceptional zero-density cases must be defined.
Detailed balance is a measure identity, not merely a pointwise density calculation.
Cold-start arguments require smoothing or explicit initialization bounds.

title: The Proximal Sampler
source_sections: 8.6 Implementations of the RGO and Applications (p. 218)
goal: Study an augmented-variable sampler that isolates difficult geometry in a proximal subproblem.
core_definitions: The proximal sampler alternates two conditionals of a Gaussian-augmented joint law.
A restricted Gaussian oracle samples a potential tilted by a local quadratic.
Simultaneous flow couples the target and auxiliary conditional evolutions.
Time reversal provides a second route to contraction and comparison.
major_results: The augmentation preserves the desired target as a marginal.
The proximal chain contracts under strong log-concavity.
Simultaneous flow and time reversal extend the analysis to general log-concavity.
Functional inequalities and implementable RGO constructions yield further convergence and application results.

calculation_route.title: Introduce a Gaussian bridge
calculation_route.explanation: Alternating the two conditional distributions creates a kernel with the desired marginal.

rigorous_details: Both conditional distributions require finite, measurable normalizing constants.
Marginal preservation follows from Tonelli/Fubini only after nonnegativity and measurability are established.
An oracle specification must state whether samples are exact or approximate.

title: Lower Bounds for Sampling
source_sections: 9.1 A Brief Discussion of Query Complexity (p. 228)
goal: Identify which dimension, smoothness, condition-number, and accuracy dependences are unavoidable.
core_definitions: Query complexity counts oracle evaluations rather than bit-level computation.
A hard family is a collection of target potentials that agree on much of the oracle transcript.
A testing reduction turns an accurate sampler into an estimator of the hidden hard-instance index.
major_results: One-dimensional constructions yield nontrivial smooth log-concave sampling lower bounds.
Constant-dimensional packings show additional accuracy and query barriers.
Gaussian families isolate dimension-dependent lower bounds in a tractable subclass.
The lower bounds calibrate which upper-bound dependences are algorithmic losses and which are intrinsic.

calculation_route.title: Encode a testing problem
calculation_route.formula: \text{sampling accuracy}\Longrightarrow\text{ability to distinguish a packed family}.
calculation_route.explanation: A sampler that is too fast would solve a statistically impossible identification problem.

rigorous_details: The oracle transcript and algorithmic randomization must be represented explicitly.
Pairwise divergence bounds need the exact observation law.
The hard family must remain inside the stated target class.

title: Structured sampling
goal: Adapt Langevin analysis to stochastic gradients, coordinate updates, and mirror geometry.
core_definitions: A stochastic-gradient oracle returns an unbiased or controlled-bias gradient estimate with a variance contract.
Coordinate methods update selected components according to a sampling schedule.
Mirror Langevin replaces Euclidean geometry by a convex mirror map and its dual coordinates.
major_results: Stochastic-gradient Langevin bounds separate oracle noise from discretization and mixing error.
Coordinate samplers exploit anisotropic smoothness through nonuniform update frequencies.
Mirror Langevin transfers continuous and discrete analysis to non-Euclidean geometry.
Each structured method exposes an oracle- or geometry-specific complexity bound.

calculation_route.title: Separate stochastic-gradient noise
calculation_route.explanation: Conditional centering removes the first-order bias, while the conditional second moment contributes a distinct error term.

calculation_route.title: Exploit coordinate smoothness
calculation_route.explanation: Sampling the coordinate and tuning its step size to coordinate-wise smoothness can avoid a worst-direction global step size.

calculation_route.title: Move to mirror coordinates
calculation_route.explanation: The mirror map transfers the dynamics to dual coordinates where the target geometry may be better conditioned.

rigorous_details: Stochastic-gradient unbiasedness and variance bounds are conditional statements with a specified filtration or kernel.
Coordinate schedules, coordinate-dependent step sizes, and anisotropic norms must be measurable and retained in constants.
Mirror maps need an open effective domain, invertible gradient map, and boundary/nonexplosion control for the transformed diffusion.
Oracle error, discretization error, and continuous-time convergence remain separate terms.
blockers: Coordinate-update kernel and anisotropic smoothness chain
recommended_order: Fix the oracle or coordinate schedule
Prove its conditional moment and measurability contracts
Track continuous, oracle, and discretization errors separately
Study mirror geometry only after the Euclidean interfaces are clear

title: Non-Log-Concave Sampling
source_sections: 11.1 Approximate First-Order Stationarity via Fisher Information (p. 267)
goal: Use Fisher information to formulate and analyze approximate stationarity for non-log-concave targets, then compare upper and lower bounds.
core_definitions: Relative Fisher information measures the squared score mismatch against the target.
Approximate first-order stationarity is formulated through small Fisher information rather than small sampling distance.
Dissipativity controls the drift outside a bounded region without global convexity.
major_results: Small Fisher information provides a meaningful stationarity certificate for non-log-concave targets.
Langevin and related algorithms admit finite-time Fisher-information bounds under stated regularity and moment assumptions.
Fisher-information control yields consequences for optimization and sampling observables.
Lower bounds delimit the attainable stationarity rates.

calculation_route.title: Use entropy dissipation as an averaged stationarity bound
calculation_route.explanation: Even without log-concavity, integrated Fisher information can decay because relative entropy is nonnegative.

calculation_route.title: Randomize an output time
calculation_route.explanation: A randomized iterate turns the time average into a stationarity guarantee.

calculation_route.title: Add algorithmic error
calculation_route.explanation: Each additional term needs its own moment, regularity, and law-comparison estimate.

rigorous_details: Relative Fisher information needs an absolutely continuous law and a chosen score representative.
Entropy dissipation must be justified for the actual process and function domain, not only calculated formally.
Randomized-time output requires measurability of the time-indexed law and Fisher-information integrand.
Finite-time discretization and score-error bounds must specify the law under which every squared error is integrated.
Small Fisher information is a stationarity certificate, not automatically small total variation or rapid multimodal mixing.
recommended_order: Define relative Fisher information and its representatives
Keep stationarity guarantees separate from global mixing claims

title: Diffusion Generative Models
goal: Connect sampling analysis to score-based reverse diffusions and generative modeling.
core_definitions: The forward diffusion progressively smooths the data law into a tractable reference law.
The score is the spatial gradient of a chosen log-density representative.
The reverse-time SDE uses the marginal score to transport noise back toward data.
Score matching rewrites inaccessible score regression as an estimable objective.
major_results: Time reversal identifies the exact reverse drift under regular marginal densities.
Implicit and denoising score-matching objectives recover the score in population form.
Generation error decomposes into initialization, score approximation, and time-discretization terms.
Discretization analysis converts integrated score error into terminal distribution error under explicit law and regularity assumptions.

calculation_route.title: Noise forward, transport backward
calculation_route.formula: dX_t=b_t(X_t)dt+\sigma_t dB_t\quad\leadsto\quad d\bar X_t=\bar b_t(\bar X_t)dt+\sigma_{T-t}d\bar B_t.
calculation_route.explanation: The reverse drift contains the score of the time marginal; approximation quality becomes a drift-error problem.

calculation_route.title: Decompose generation error
calculation_route.explanation: Each term has different regularity and data requirements.

rigorous_details: A score is defined only with respect to a chosen density and representative.
Reverse-time formulas require time-marginal regularity and a precise filtration statement.
An L2 score approximation under one law cannot silently be used under another law.
recommended_order: Fix the forward process and its marginals
Then separate reversal, score, and numerical errors
